# simpledir

> Named directory shortcuts for the shell. The next zoxide: no frecency
> database, no daemon, no shell-injection. One JSON file of `name -> path`
> plus a small shell function that performs the `cd`.

A single-file Python 3.8+ command line tool with zero dependencies. It stores
aliases you name yourself, and jumps to the bound directory. Useful when the
same dozen directories are visited every day and you want them to have names.
Complements, does not replace, [zoxide](https://github.com/ajeetdsouza/zoxide).

## Docs

- [README.md](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/README.md): full documentation
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/AGENTS.md): notes for coding agents working on this repository
- [CONTRIBUTORS.md](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/CONTRIBUTORS.md): authorship and how to contribute
- [LICENSE](https://github.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/blob/main/LICENSE): MIT

## Install

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/main/install.sh | bash
```

The installer checks for Python 3.8+, installs it with yay, pacman or mise (in
that order) if missing, downloads the `simpledir` release asset into
`~/.local/bin`, and appends a guarded wrapper block to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`
(chosen from `$SHELL`). Re-running it refreshes the block and keeps a backup.
`bash install.sh --uninstall` reverses all of it.

From source: `git clone … && make install`.

## Commands

```
simpledir add [<name>] [<path>]  bind an alias; name defaults to the directory's basename, path to $PWD; -f overwrites
simpledir rm <name>              remove an alias
simpledir rename <old> <new>     change an alias's name, keeping its path; -f overwrites
simpledir import <dir>           bind every subdirectory of a tree; -d/--depth (default 1), -p/--prefix, -f/--force, --hidden, -n/--dry-run
simpledir ls [<query>] [-l]      list aliases; <query> filters on name or path substring; -l forces absolute paths
simpledir ls --names             one alias per line, no padding, for completion scripts
simpledir ls --json              JSON object of the same shape as the config file
simpledir jump <alias[/sub]>     print the bound path to stdout, do not cd
simpledir edit [<editor>]        open the config in $EDITOR (default), creating an empty one if absent
simpledir update                 check for a newer release, ask, then install it; --check reports only (exit 1 if an update exists); -y/--yes skips the prompt
simpledir doctor                 report config, dead aliases, shell wiring and PATH problems; exit 1 if any
simpledir completions bash|zsh   print a shell completion script
simpledir init                   print the shell wrapper to append to a shell rc file
simpledir <alias>                in a shell: jump. elsewhere: same as `jump`
```

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` unknown alias or user error, `2` argument parsing
error (argparse).

An alias argument may carry a path suffix: `dots/src` resolves to `<dots>/src`.
Suffixes are normalized with `normpath`, so `dots/src/..` and `dots/` both work.
The shell wrapper also accepts a raw path: `sd /some/path` just `cd`s.

## Shell wrapper

`sd <name>` and `simpledir <name>` `cd`. This is done by shell functions emitted
by `simpledir init`, because a subprocess cannot change the calling shell's
working directory. The `simpledir` function shadows the binary, intercepting only
bare aliases; `add`, `rm`, `ls`, `jump`, `init` and flags are forwarded to the
real binary via `command simpledir`.

- `sd` with no arguments: `cd $HOME`
- `sd -`: `cd $OLDPWD`
- `sd dots/src`: `cd` into a subdirectory of a bound alias

Functions rather than shell aliases, because bash expands aliases only in
interactive shells.

## Configuration

Path: `~/.simpledir/config.json`. Override the directory with the
`SIMPLEDIR_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable. The file is plain JSON and safe to
edit by hand.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "aliases": {
    "dots": "/home/you/dotfiles",
    "hypr": "/home/you/.config/hypr"
  }
}
```

Schema: `version` is an integer, currently `1`. `aliases` maps a non-empty alias
name to an absolute directory path. Writes are atomic: temporary file plus
`os.replace`.

## Behavior on errors

- unknown alias: message with substring and `difflib` suggestions, exit `1`
- alias or alias-with-suffix resolving to a missing directory: `jump` refuses and
  explains how to rebind; `ls` tags it `[missing]`
- duplicate alias: refused unless `--force` is given, for both `add` and `rename`
- corrupt or unreadable config: explains the problem, suggests removal, does not
  silently reset
- `ls` with no aliases: usage hint on stderr, exit `1`
- `ls <query>` with no match: says so, exit `1`
- unknown flag: argparse usage error, exit `2`
- `update` when GitHub is unreachable: says so, exit `1`
- `update` never replaces a binary with a same-version or unidentifiable download

## Update mechanism

`update` fetches `https://api.github.com/repos/noxthedevwindev-greatest/simpledir/releases/latest`,
compares `tag_name` against `VERSION`, and on a newer tag downloads the release
asset `simpledir`, runs it with `--version` to confirm identity and version, then
writes it next to the target and `os.replace`s it into place.

Additionally, `add` and `ls` may print a one-line nudge to stderr when a newer
release is known. It is suppressed when stderr is not a terminal, when
`SIMPLEDIR_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` is set, when the cache in
`~/.simpledir/update-check.json` is younger than 24 hours, and never on the
`jump` path.

Environment variables:

```
SIMPLEDIR_CONFIG_DIR       config directory                (default ~/.simpledir)
SIMPLEDIR_NO_UPDATE_CHECK  set to anything to disable update checks
SIMPLEDIR_BIN              override the path `update` writes to
SIMPLEDIR_UPDATE_URL       override the release API URL (used by the test suite)
SIMPLEDIR_UPDATE_ASSET_URL override the downloaded asset URL (used by the test suite)
```

## Version history

- 3.0.0 — one-command `curl | bash` installer that resolves python through
  yay/pacman/mise, `update` with verification and atomic self-install, a quiet
  once-a-day update nudge, `import` for bulk binding, `doctor` for install
  health, and downloadable release assets. Config format unchanged at
  `version: 1`.
- 2.0.0 — path suffixes on alias arguments, `rename`, `add` with fewer
  arguments, `edit`, `ls` filtering, `ls --names`, `ls --json`, shell
  completions. Config format unchanged at `version: 1`.
- 1.0.0 — `add`, `rm`, `ls`, `jump`, `init`, the shell wrapper, typo
  suggestions, atomic config writes.

## Development

```
make test     # 145 assertions, runs real bash subprocesses
make assets   # build dist/ (simpledir + install.sh, mode 755)
make release  # tag from VERSION, push, publish with assets
vhs docs/demo.tape   # re-record docs/demo.gif (needs vhs and ttyd)
```

Repository layout:

```
simpledir          the entire tool, one executable Python file
install.sh         the curl | bash installer
tests/run.sh       test suite, plain bash
docs/demo.tape     vhs script that produces docs/demo.gif
packaging/PKGBUILD Arch package definition
Makefile           install / uninstall / test / assets / release targets
```
